import numpy as np

# Get grasp pose for the red cube and grasp it with an approach from above
grasp_pos, grasp_quat = sample_grasp_pose("red cube")
open_gripper()
goto_pose(grasp_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.1)
close_gripper()

# Lift the red cube straight up to avoid collisions
lift_pos = grasp_pos.copy()
lift_pos[2] += 0.15
goto_pose(lift_pos, grasp_quat)

# Get poses and extents of both cubes
red_pos, _, red_extent = get_object_pose("red cube", return_bbox_extent=True)
green_pos, _, green_extent = get_object_pose("green cube", return_bbox_extent=True)

# Compute placement: red cube center should be at green top + half red height.
# The gripper was at grasp_pos when red cube center was at red_pos (before lifting),
# so keep the same gripper-to-cube-center offset in z.
# Use original grasp_pos relative to the red cube's original position for the offset.
orig_red_pos = grasp_pos  # approximate; refine with the offset below
gripper_offset_z = grasp_pos[2] - (red_pos[2] - 0.15) if abs(red_pos[2] - (grasp_pos[2] + 0.15)) < 0.1 else 0.0

target_center_z = green_pos[2] + green_extent[2] / 2.0 + red_extent[2] / 2.0
place_pos = np.array([green_pos[0], green_pos[1], target_center_z + gripper_offset_z])

# Move above the green cube first, then descend gently to the placement height
goto_pose(place_pos, grasp_quat, z_approach=0.1)

# Release the cube gently (it is already resting on the green cube)
open_gripper()

# Retreat upward
retreat_pos = place_pos.copy()
retreat_pos[2] += 0.1
goto_pose(retreat_pos, grasp_quat)
